title: KV thermal equalizer and slot-stitcher: reduce fragmentation and relocation churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket implements a two-part allocator improvement designed to reduce KV-cache fragmentation and relocation churn under continuous-batching workloads. The approach combines (1) a lightweight per-GPU thermal-equalizer score used to guide allocation and preemptive rehoming decisions, and (2) a slot-stitcher background operation that opportunistically merges adjacent free fragments into larger contiguous ranges without long pauses to serving. Goal: lower live relocation frequency by 30–50% for tail-burst traffic while preserving batch throughput and latency SLOs.
problem_statement: Continuous batching plus high token churn creates many small free gaps in GPU KV pools. These micro-fragments force frequent relocations of long-lived KV entries (causing latency spikes and higher memory copies) or lead to overprovisioned pools to compensate. Existing compaction strategies are either too aggressive (impacting latency) or too lazy (allowing fragmentation to grow).
proposal_summary: Introduce a thermal-equalizer allocator that tracks short-term occupancy, access churn, and eviction pressure per micro-region, then biases new allocations to zones with low churn; implement a low-impact slot-stitcher that performs many tiny merges spread across epochs with adaptive backoff so compaction work never interferes with hot-path batches. Combine with an epoched lease for recently-moved tokens to avoid immediate re-relocation.
milestones: Prototype thermal score collector (unit tests + microbench) - week 1
Integrate allocation bias into runtime allocator - week 2
Slot-stitcher background loop + adaptive backoff - week 3
Canary on internal dedicated cluster + dashboards - week 4
Gradual rollout with feature flag - week 5
acceptance_criteria: Relocation count per 1M requests reduced >= 30% on internal mixed-batch trace compared to baseline
p95 tail latency change < 5% for inference tokens under canary traffic
Compaction CPU/GPU overhead stays below 4% of node budget under steady-state
No increase in memory OOM incidents during canary rollout
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged merge to main behind runtime config (thermal_equalizer=true)
Canary on low-traffic dedicated pool (internal) for 72h
Observe metrics and increase canary size to 10% of production read load
Enable on all dedicated pools with gradual ramp and safety rollback if p95 > threshold
test_plan: Unit tests for thermal score decay and allocation bias
Synthetic microbench that simulates continuous-batching churn (replay trace) to assert relocation delta
End-to-end canary harness with traffic replay and chaos (preemptive memory pressure)
implementation_notes: Thermal score: exponentially-weighted moving average combining occupancy, recent eviction rate, and access variance; kept per-64KB micro-region to reduce metadata overhead
Slot-stitcher: cooperative background worker with tokenized checkpoints to allow preemption; merges are limited by a budget of bytes/sec and adaptive backoff when batch latency climbs
Epoched lease: moved entries are given a short lease (N allocations) preventing immediate re-relocation to oscillate between regions
tradeoffs_and_risks: Biasing allocations can cause hotlets to clump — mitigated by including access-variance into score
Background stitching adds CPU/GPU cycles; budgeted and limited by adaptive backoff
Incorrect decay constants could underreact/overreact — will tune via lab traces
